sentences.text: Blikanasaurus was a sauropodomorph dinosaur with heavily built hindlimb bones, unusually thick ankles, and large phalanges. This animal is estimated to have reached lengths between three and five meters.

The genus name Blikanasaurus means "lizard from Blikana" in Greek, while the species name cromptoni honors American paleontologist A.W. "Fuzz" Crompton. The first fossils were discovered at the foot of Blikana mountain in Herschel, Eastern Cape, South Africa.

The genus is known only from partial hindlimb bones found in the lower Elliot Formation. A second specimen, consisting of a right metatarsal, was recovered in the early 2000s from the Damplaats farm in the eastern Free State.
A recently found possible ilium has been attributed to Blikanasaurus, but this attribution remains unconfirmed.
Researchers hypothesize that Blikanasaurus was an obligate quadruped due to its robust build.
Blikanasaurus is currently classified as a basal sauropodomorph, though little is known due to incomplete fossils.
Some paleontologists proposed grouping Blikanasaurus in the family Blikanasauridae, but this family has not been formally accepted.
Blikanasaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa. It lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
It has been suggested that Blikanasaurus might be a synonym of Euskelosaurus.
